answer: Each agent identity must lock a bond in a kernel escrow before its vote counts. The escrow accepts funds only through one declared inlet per member, and a trellis of mutual vouchers links accounts so no clone can inherit a neighbor's standing. A shared inlet or a voucher loop slashes every bond in the cycle. To buy N votes an attacker must post N full bonds, and once the trellis reveals the common funding source all of them are forfeited, so the cost grows linearly with the number of fake identities.
